body_pages.reason: Abstract and Introduction (page 0) through Conclusion and Discussion (page 9); excludes the references (end of page 9 to page 12) and Appendix A (pages 13-41: other RL attempts, idea examples, code execution trajectories).

key_points.text: The authors build an automated executor that implements LLM-generated research ideas as code and runs large-scale parallel GPU experiments to verify their effectiveness.
key_points.evidence_quote: we first build an automated executor to implement ideas and launch large-scale parallel GPU experiments to verify their effectiveness

key_points.text: Earlier expert-review studies by Si et al. found LLM research ideas often look convincing but prove ineffective once executed, motivating execution-grounded idea generation.
key_points.evidence_quote: found that LLM ideas often look convincing but are ineffective after being executed by human researchers.

key_points.text: During execution-guided search, only Claude-4.5-Opus shows a clear scaling curve over epochs; Claude-4.5-Sonnet and GPT-5 tend to saturate early.
key_points.evidence_quote: when analyzing the scaling trend, only Claude-4.5-Opus shows a clear scaling curve, while both Claude-4.5-Sonnet and GPT-5 tend to saturate early.

key_points.text: The study uses two open-ended research environments: LLM pre-training (speeding up a nanoGPT speedrun baseline) and post-training (improving a GRPO math-reasoning baseline).
key_points.evidence_quote: In this work, we construct both a pre-training environment and a post-training environment for the automated AI researchers to work on.

key_points.text: Within ten search epochs, execution-guided search finds a post-training recipe that outperforms the GRPO baseline.
key_points.evidence_quote: Within ten search epochs, this execution-guided search finds a post-training recipe that outperforms the GRPO baseline

key_points.text: A large fraction of sampled ideas execute successfully; Claude-4.5-Opus and Claude-4.5-Sonnet have significantly higher execution rates than GPT-5.
key_points.evidence_quote: a large fraction of the sampled ideas can indeed be executed successfully, with Claude-4.5-Opus and Claude-4.5-Sonnet having a significantly higher execution rate than GPT-5.

key_points.text: On post-training, Claude-4.5-Sonnet's search found that vanilla policy gradient with a group-average baseline, without importance reweighting or clipping, beat the standard GRPO objective in this setup.
key_points.evidence_quote: Claude-4.5-Sonnet finds that using vanilla policy gradient with the group-average baseline without importance reweighting or clipping outperforms the standard GRPO objective

key_points.text: The top pre-training solution found by search reaches the target validation loss significantly faster than the nanoGPT baseline codebase.
key_points.evidence_quote: and it reaches the 3.28 target validation loss in 19.7 minutes, a significant speedup as compared to the baseline codebase

key_points.text: The best human nanoGPT speedrun solution remains far faster, which the authors read as significant headroom for better models and search methods.
key_points.evidence_quote: indicating significant headroom for further model capability and search method improvement on this environment.

key_points.text: Under the same sampling budget, execution-guided search beat best-of-N in the authors' nanoGPT comparison, which they take as evidence of learning from earlier trajectories.
key_points.evidence_quote: demonstrating that the model is effectively leveraging trajectories from previous epochs to generate more effective ideas in future epochs.

key_points.text: Reinforcement learning with execution reward raises the average performance of generated ideas over training epochs in these open-ended research environments.
key_points.evidence_quote: that the average performance of the generated ideas can increase after sufficient training epochs for open-ended research environments

key_points.text: However, the max reward, which the authors argue matters most for discovery, fluctuates throughout RL training without a clear upward trend.
key_points.evidence_quote: the max reward is fluctuating throughout RL training without a clear upward trend. This reveals the crucial limitation of the standard GRPO algorithm

key_points.text: RL makes the ideator collapse onto a few simple-to-implement ideas with shrinking thinking traces, raising average reward but not the upper bound.
key_points.evidence_quote: The above analyses reveal that RL causes the models to converge on a few simple-to-implement ideas

key_points.text: The authors argue that avoiding the convergence and collapse seen in RL is an open problem likely needing new algorithmic interventions beyond standard GRPO.
key_points.evidence_quote: Avoiding such convergence and collapse is an open problem and likely requires new algorithmic interventions beyond standard GRPO

key_points.text: The authors caution that their procedure does not test generalizability: the best small-scale ideas may not transfer to larger scales or other datasets.
key_points.evidence_quote: It is possible that the best-performing ideas at the small scales may not transfer to gains at a larger scale or on other datasets.
